section_title: Standardized Dry Bulk & Tanker Secondhand Benchmark Prices vs Newbuilding Replacement Parity
section_path_text: Valuations > S&P Asset Prices > Dry Bulk & Tankers
text: August 2026 secondhand asset valuations vs newbuilding replacement parity: Capesize (180k DWT): Newbuild .5m, 5Y .5m, 10Y .0m, 15Y .5m, Scrap Demolition .8m. 5-year-old Capesize prices stand at 88.2% of newbuild cost (vs historical 72% median), driven by prompt earnings yield (20.0% annualized charter yield at ,000/day 1Y TC). Newcastlemax (210k DWT): Newbuild .0m, 5Y .5m (88.7% ratio). Kamsarmax (82k DWT): Newbuild .5m, 5Y .2m (88.8% ratio). VLCC (300k DWT): Newbuild .5m, 5Y .0m, 10Y .0m, 15Y .0m, Scrap .9m (5Y/NB ratio: 88.8%, 17.5% charter yield). Suezmax (160k DWT): Newbuild .0m, 5Y .5m (89.2% ratio). Secondhand asset values across both wet and dry sectors trade at 15-year highs due to 3-year shipyard backlog delivery constraints.
